clue.text: Surveillance is the consequence of a broken roof?

definitions.text: the consequence of a broken roof

blocks.note: first meaning: secretly listening in on others

blocks.clueFragment: the consequence of a broken roof
blocks.note: second, punning meaning: water dripping off the edge of a damaged roof

explanation.surface: A spy notes that being watched is what you get when your roof caves in.
explanation.walkthrough: The eaves are the overhanging lower edge of a roof; split the answer into EAVES DROPPING and a broken roof would do exactly that.
explanation.definitionFit: Listening secretly to private conversation is a form of covert monitoring, so it counts as surveillance.

clue.text: Small fairies might be the kings of rock 'n' roll?

blocks.note: first meaning: little mischievous sprites of folklore
second, punning meaning: a plural of Elvis Presley's first name, he being the King of Rock 'n' Roll

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the joke plural: more than one Elvis would be a group of these creatures.
explanation.definitionFit: Elves are diminutive magical beings from folklore, a kind of tiny fairy.

clue.text: Courage, Virginia! Oregon is just past trail's end

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter only
being just past something means coming straight after it in the word

blocks.note: VA is the US postal abbreviation for the state
the final letter of the word
OR is the US postal abbreviation for the state

explanation.surface: A pioneer is urged to be brave: Oregon lies just beyond the end of the trail.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oregon Trail was the pioneers' wagon route west, so the surface reads as a frontier pep talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Valor, the American spelling of valour, is bravery in the face of danger, a synonym of courage.

clue.text: After reorganization, Sony covers New York with my identity

indicators.note: reorganizing puts things in a new order, so the brand's letters are rearranged
in a down entry, covering means sitting on top, so this piece comes first

blocks.note: the electronics brand, taken as fodder
NY is the standard abbreviation
taken as written

explanation.surface: After a corporate restructuring, Sony expands into New York and claims an identity.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonymy is sameness of meaning between words, so it is a kind of identity.

clue.text: Witherspoon looking up online prophet?

indicators.note: in a down entry, looking up means the letters are read from bottom to top

blocks.note: E- is the prefix for electronic, as in e-mail
a seer foresees the future

explanation.surface: A question whether the actress has been consulting a fortune-teller on the internet.
explanation.walkthrough: Reese Witherspoon is the American actress; 'looking up' sounds like searching online.
explanation.definitionFit: Reese is the first name of the film actress Reese Witherspoon, so her surname leads straight to it.

clue.text: Depicted unsatisfactory deal for speakers

indicators.note: for speakers means as heard when spoken, so the sound counts, not the spelling

blocks.note: a bad bargain is a poor trade

explanation.surface: A description of a bad bargain, pitched to an audience.
explanation.definitionFit: To portray someone is to represent them in art or words, so the past tense matches depicted.

clue.text: If incorporated, sea change comes next

indicators.note: a change alters the order, so the preceding three letters are rearranged
coming next means this piece follows straight after the first

blocks.note: Inc. is the abbreviation used after American company names
taken as fodder

explanation.surface: A sea change, a profound transformation, follows once a firm is incorporated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sea change' reads as one idiom meaning a big transformation; it splits into fodder and a mixing signal.
explanation.definitionFit: In case can mean if, as in 'in case of fire, break glass'.

clue.text: Musician's taut rig is disassembled

indicators.note: something disassembled is taken apart and could be rebuilt in any order

blocks.note: nine letters of fodder

explanation.surface: A performer's tight equipment rig gets dismantled after the gig.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is short for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay rather than marking possession.
explanation.definitionFit: A guitarist plays the guitar, so is one kind of instrumental performer.

clue.text: Someone who finishes bathroom in purple?

blocks.note: lav is British slang for a lavatory
one who ends something

explanation.surface: A decorator who completes a bathroom in a purple colour scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces are read in reverse clue order: the bathroom word comes first in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lavender is a pale purple shade named after the flower, so it is a type of purple.

clue.text: Offer to revel un-orgiastically

indicators.note: an orgy is wild and disorderly, so the letters before it are thrown into a jumble

blocks.note: the nine letters of 'to revel' plus the 'un' hyphenated onto the indicator

explanation.surface: An invitation to party, but in a restrained, decidedly non-orgiastic way.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'un-' looks like part of the adjective, but its two letters belong to the fodder, leaving 'orgiastically' as the mixing signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To volunteer is to put yourself forward freely, which is a synonym of the verb offer.

clue.text: What Jay Leno is known for: high-grade porcelain

blocks.clueFragment: What Jay Leno is known for
blocks.note: the US talk-show host is famous for his prominent jaw
A is the top grade on a school report

explanation.surface: A quiz-style question about a TV host's trademark, answered with fine tableware.
explanation.walkthrough: Jay Leno hosted America's Tonight Show and his jutting jaw was a running joke.
explanation.definitionFit: China is the everyday name for fine ceramic tableware, a synonym of porcelain.

clue.text: Bizarre, unusual garnets

indicators.note: something unusual is out of its normal form, so the following word's letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the gemstones, taken letter for letter as fodder

explanation.surface: A jeweller describes some odd-looking red gemstones.
explanation.definitionFit: Strange and bizarre are near synonyms, both meaning weird or out of the ordinary.

clue.text: Those who remained had to report once again

blocks.note: the rest are the ones left over
had a meal, as in 'had lunch'

explanation.surface: The survivors of some ordeal were made to give their account a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Had' looks like an auxiliary with 'to', but it is a verb of eating.
explanation.definitionFit: To restate is to say or set out again, which is repeating a report.

clue.text: Ay! In a bad way

blocks.note: a description of how the word is written: a capital A standing beside a lowercase, or small, y

explanation.surface: A cry of anguish from someone who is clearly in a sorry state.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer, read as four separate words, describes how the exclamation looks in print, so the wordplay lies in the answer rather than the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Abysmally means dreadfully or appallingly, so it describes doing something terribly badly.

clue.text: Pretended to hold up kiss — for the most part, that's OK

indicators.note: most of something means it loses its final letter
in a down entry, up means the letters run from bottom to top
holding something means wrapping around it

blocks.note: acted as in put on a show, feigned
a peck is a quick light kiss

explanation.surface: Someone faked holding back a kiss, and claims it was mostly fine.
explanation.definitionFit: Accepted means approved or regarded as proper, a synonym of OK used as an adjective.

clue.text: With audio application, "amend" becomes "amen"

blocks.note: surface reading: a sound-editing app clips the last letter of a word
setter's reading: a spoken phrase that does the same job as the word of agreement said at the end of a prayer

explanation.walkthrough: The app picture suggests editing software; the real idea is a spoken phrase that stands for 'amen', the word of hearty agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: Amen is used informally to express strong agreement, just like the spoken interjection meaning 'I agree entirely'.

clue.text: Three-quarters fat, one quarter that's needy and slow

indicators.note: three quarters of a four-letter word keeps three letters and loses the last

blocks.note: lard is pig fat used in cooking
a poor, deprived district of a city

explanation.surface: A recipe of fractions: mostly fat, a quarter of it needy and sluggish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quarter' is used twice: first as a fraction, then as a district of a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Larghetto is the musical tempo marking for fairly slow, a little quicker than largo.

clue.text: Discovery is subjected to a penalty at a hearing

indicators.note: a hearing is something listened to, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: being fined is being given a money penalty

explanation.surface: A court hearing where a new piece of evidence ends with someone being penalised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearing' sounds legal, suiting the penalty, but it signals the sound of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A find is a thing that has been found, so as a noun it is a synonym of discovery.

clue.text: Infielders on team originally in cellar

indicators.note: originally points to the origin, the first letter of the word
in a down entry, being on something means sitting above it, so it comes first

blocks.note: first, second and third basemen are baseball infielders
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: The baseball team's infielders first gathered in a cellar.
explanation.walkthrough: In baseball the infield is guarded by the first, second and third basemen.
explanation.definitionFit: A basement is the storey below ground level, a synonym for a cellar.

clue.text: This signal left within

indicators.note: within says the next letter sits inside the word before it

blocks.note: a cue is a signal to begin
L is the standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A terse instruction about a sign that was left inside somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This' refers to the very thing the solver is reading: the clue itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The self-referential 'This' points at the text being read, which is itself a crossword clue.

clue.text: Fire ant, perhaps, consuming the head of Andrew McCarthy, famously

indicators.note: consuming means swallowing, so one part goes inside the other
the head of a word is its first letter alone

blocks.note: the fire ant is a red insect that bites, so jokingly a red biter
the first letter of the name

explanation.surface: A fire ant swallowing the head of someone called Andrew McCarthy, apparently a well-known incident.
explanation.walkthrough: Andrew McCarthy reads as one person, but the surname belongs to the definition: Senator Joseph McCarthy, who hunted alleged Communists in 1950s America.
explanation.definitionFit: A red-baiter attacks people as Communists; Joseph McCarthy is the most notorious example of one.

clue.text: Alter course of Southern fighter in Balkan capital

blocks.note: to zag is to change direction sharply, as in zigzag
Johnny Reb was the nickname for a Confederate soldier in the American Civil War

explanation.surface: A Confederate soldier changes course while in a European capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Zagreb is the capital city of Croatia, a country on the Balkan peninsula.

clue.text: Discussed Mia with autocrat

indicators.note: something discussed is spoken about, so the word comes by its spoken sound

blocks.note: Mia leads to the surname of the actress Mia Farrow

explanation.surface: Gossip about an actress and her meeting with a dictator.
explanation.walkthrough: The first name stands in for the surname of the Hollywood actress Mia Farrow, which is said just like the Egyptian ruler's title.
explanation.definitionFit: A pharaoh was an ancient Egyptian king with absolute power, so an example of an autocrat.

clue.text: Bloke largely gets around other section of London

indicators.note: largely means most but not all, so the word before loses its final letter
getting around something means surrounding it, so one part encloses the other

blocks.note: chap is informal British for a man
else means other, as in 'someone else'

explanation.surface: A man travels round a different part of the city.
explanation.walkthrough: Chelsea is an affluent district of west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Chelsea is a named district within the London borough of Kensington and Chelsea, an example of an area of the city.

clue.text: Red wine in a stateroom

blocks.note: cab is short for cabernet sauvignon
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is drinking red wine in their private room on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' reads as a preposition but contributes its own two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A stateroom is a private sleeping room on a ship or train, the same thing as a cabin.

clue.text: Internally embellish a Korean military hat

indicators.note: internally means on the inside, so the letters sit inside the following words

blocks.note: the run of letters across the boundaries of the three words

explanation.surface: An instruction to decorate a Korean army cap on the inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A shako is a tall, peaked cylindrical cap with a plume, worn by soldiers in dress uniform.

clue.text: One lodge member getting high with joint

indicators.note: in a down entry, getting high means rising, so the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: an is the indefinite article, meaning one
a member of the Elks, an American fraternal order that meets in lodges

explanation.surface: A member of a social club gets stoned on a marijuana cigarette.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' and 'getting high' suggest cannabis; the joint is a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: The ankle is the hinge connecting foot to leg, one of the body's joints.

clue.text: Senior metalworker starts late

indicators.note: starting late means missing the beginning, so the opening letter is dropped

blocks.note: a welder joins metal pieces with heat

explanation.surface: An older tradesman in a metal shop turns up late for his shift.
explanation.definitionFit: An elder is a person older than another, so the noun is a synonym of senior.

clue.text: At first, Kirkland follows dancing at ballet with informal conversation

indicators.note: dancing moves things around, so the following letters swap places
at first means only the opening letter of the name is used
follows says the selected piece comes after the other part

blocks.note: the eight letters taken as fodder
the first letter of the surname

explanation.surface: The ballerina Gelsey Kirkland chats after dancing at the ballet.
explanation.walkthrough: Gelsey Kirkland was a famous American ballerina, which makes 'dancing at ballet' read naturally rather than as a signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Table talk is relaxed chat around a meal table, a synonym for casual conversation.

clue.text: Existential question latent in Brontë's letters

annotation.answer: TO BE OR NOT TO BE

blocks.note: surface reading: a deep philosophical query about life, of the kind found in Victorian novels
setter's reading: the famous question can be spelt using only the six different letters of the novelist's surname

explanation.surface: A literary scholar finds a philosophical question hidden in a Brontë sister's correspondence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letters' suggests correspondence, but means the alphabet letters B, R, O, N, T, E, which are the only ones Hamlet's soliloquy opening uses.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet's line asks whether to go on living, the most famous question about existence itself.
